profile.campus: Manassas, Prince William County, Virginia (QTS Manassas campus)
profile.reading:
Per QTS's own site, Manassas DC1 sits at 9400 Godwin Dr, Manassas, VA 20110, part of a planned six-building, 105-acre campus with 190+ MW of critical campus capacity upon completion. This registry carries two separate OSM entries both named QTS Manassas DC1 (this row and osm:way/1464257784), most likely a duplicate map entity; both are documented identically per this project's never-delete/never-merge policy pending manual OSM de-duplication.

QTS Data Centers (shown on this row under its pre-2013-IPO name, "Quality Technology Services") was founded in 2003 in Overland Park, Kansas. Per Blackstone's own press release, Blackstone Real Estate Income Trust (BREIT) and other Blackstone-affiliated funds completed a roughly $10 billion acquisition of QTS Realty Trust on August 31, 2021, taking the company private at $78 per share; QTS is no longer an independent SEC filer. QTS's own site lists its US headquarters at 22271 Broderick Drive, Sterling, Virginia, placing this Northern Virginia "Data Center Alley" corridor, alongside neighboring hyperscale and colocation campuses from Amazon, Equinix, Digital Realty, and CyrusOne, at the center of the company's operations.

Dominion Energy, the dominant electric utility across Northern Virginia's data center corridor, has repeatedly cited data center demand growth as a primary driver of its long-term transmission and generation planning, and Loudoun and Prince William County officials have both cited data center real estate and business-license tax revenue as a significant share of their county budgets. QTS's Virginia campuses sit within this same regional grid and policy environment as neighboring hyperscale and colocation buildings operated by Amazon, Equinix, Digital Realty, and CyrusOne, all tracked elsewhere in this registry.

QTS positions itself as a "hyperscale-neutral" wholesale and colocation landlord, leasing built capacity to enterprise, cloud, and hyperscale tenants rather than operating its own end-user cloud service, a business model shared with peers like Digital Realty and CyrusOne in this same Northern Virginia corridor; under Blackstone ownership since 2021, QTS has continued expanding its US footprint (including its Manassas and Richmond 3 campuses, both still under construction as of the facts recorded here) rather than slowing development after going private.

reading.body:
QTS Manassas DC1 is one building in a planned six-building, 105-acre campus in Prince William County with 190 MW or more of critical power capacity upon completion. The campus sits within Northern Virginia's data center corridor, where Dominion Energy has identified data center demand as a primary driver of transmission and generation planning, and where Loudoun and Prince William County officials depend on data center tax revenue as a material share of county budgets. At a typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, 190 MW of critical power represents roughly 4,750 racks as a campus total once built out, though this figure assumes all capacity is dedicated to accelerator-dense workloads rather than mixed enterprise or storage use.

This facility is currently mapped as one of 326 data centers in Virginia, but only 23 Virginia facilities publish power capacity figures. The Manassas campus's 190 MW places it at rank 24 among published Virginia facilities, representing 13.8 percent of the state's 1,375 MW of published capacity. The campus is part of QTS's Northern Virginia footprint, which spans Loudoun County, Prince William County, and Sterling alongside hyperscale and colocation peers including Amazon, Equinix, Digital Realty, and CyrusOne.

QTS operates as a wholesale and colocation landlord rather than a hyperscale cloud operator, meaning it builds and leases capacity to enterprise, cloud, and hyperscale tenants. The company was acquired by Blackstone for approximately 10 billion dollars in August 2021 and has continued expanding its Virginia campuses after going private. No certifications, power purchasing agreements, or specific tenant information are published in the operator's spec page for this site.
